seoTitle: How to Sync Google Calendar With Slack (2026)
metaDescription: Connect Google Calendar to Slack to auto-update your status during meetings, get event reminders, and respond to invites from chat.
intro: Switching over to your calendar app just to check if you're free, or missing a meeting because the reminder popped up in a tab you'd already closed, is exactly what the Google Calendar app for Slack is meant to fix. It links your schedule into Slack so your status changes automatically when you're in a meeting and event reminders show up as messages you can act on directly. This guide walks through finding the app in Slack's own Apps directory, what its listing actually promises before you install it, and the account authorization it needs to work.

steps.heading: Open the Apps section in Slack
steps.body: From the left sidebar's Tools menu, click Apps. This is the same directory used for every integration Slack supports, not a calendar-specific menu, so you'll see a general app list load before you search for anything specific. A banner near the top usually flags that adding unlimited apps is a paid-plan feature during a free trial, which is worth noting if your workspace is still on trial.

image.caption: The Apps section under Tools, the entry point for finding and installing the Google Calendar integration.

steps.heading: Search for Google Calendar
steps.body: Type "Google Calendar" into the search field at the top of the Apps page. The results split into the official Google Calendar listing at the top and a row of "Available Apps" below it — third-party calendar tools like Status Calendar, an AI meeting assistant, and Reclaim.ai that do similar but not identical things. Stick with the official Google Calendar entry if what you want is straightforward status syncing and invite handling rather than a more elaborate scheduling assistant.

image.caption: Search results for "Google Calendar," with the official app at the top and related third-party calendar tools listed underneath.

steps.heading: Open the official app listing
steps.body: Clicking the Google Calendar result opens a side panel with the app's icon, a short description — "See your schedule, respond to invites, and get event updates" — and an Open App button alongside a VIP badge. This panel is your preview before committing to anything; scroll its description section for the fuller feature breakdown before you click through to install.

image.caption: The Google Calendar app's preview panel inside Slack's Apps page, before opening the full marketplace listing.

steps.heading: Review the feature list and pricing
steps.body: The full marketplace listing spells out what the integration actually does: automatically sync your calendar to your Slack status during meetings, see a holistic view of your daily schedule from inside Slack, get notified when an event is starting and join it directly from the reminder, respond to invites without leaving chat, and get updated when an event's details change. Pricing is listed as free. The listing also notes real limits worth knowing upfront — your status won't include the meeting name, you can override the auto-set status at any time, and syncing only applies to the primary calendar on the connected Google account.

image.caption: The Google Calendar listing on Slack's marketplace, showing the Open in Slack button, supported languages, and free pricing.

steps.heading: Authorize your Google account
steps.body: Clicking Open in Slack (or Add to Slack, depending on where you launch it from) walks you through a permissions review before redirecting to Google's own sign-in and consent screen. Choose the Google account whose calendar you actually want synced — if you manage more than one Google account, it's easy to authorize the wrong one by default, so double-check the email shown before clicking Allow.

steps.heading: Turn on status syncing and test it
steps.body: Back in Slack, open the Google Calendar app's Home tab and turn on status syncing if it isn't already active. Put a short test event on your calendar a few minutes out and watch your Slack status update automatically once it starts — this confirms the connection actually works rather than just appearing configured. Remember that any status you set manually overrides the calendar sync until your next event, so it won't fight you if you need to post a custom status mid-meeting.

faq.question: Will my Slack status change automatically during a meeting?
faq.answer: Yes, once status sync is turned on, Slack updates your status and emoji based on your calendar events — though the status text won't include the meeting's name.

faq.question: Can I respond to a meeting invite from Slack?
faq.answer: Yes, event reminder messages let you respond to invites and get notified when a meeting starts directly from the chat message.

faq.question: Does this work with multiple Google Calendars?
faq.answer: No — per the app's own listing, Slack only syncs with the primary calendar on the Google account you connect, not any secondary or shared calendars.

faq.question: Can I override my synced status manually?
faq.answer: Yes, setting your own status at any time takes priority — the Google Calendar app won't overwrite a status you've set yourself.

faq.question: Is the Google Calendar app for Slack free?
faq.answer: Yes, its marketplace listing shows it as a free app with no listed pricing tier.
